status_summary: The measures found target foreign-gift disclosure rather than a funding or accreditation cutoff. Executive Order 14282 (signed 2025-04-23) directs the Education Secretary to enforce Section 117 of the Higher Education Act, requires that Section 117 compliance certification be material for False Claims Act purposes, and bars federal grants to noncompliant institutions. The Education Department opened a Section 117 investigation of UC Berkeley on 2025-04-25, relaunched its reporting portal on 2026-01-02, signed an enforcement agreement with the State Department on 2026-02-20, published new data on 2026-08-03, and was reported on 2026-09-17 to be probing Duke University and the University of North Dakota, with a State Department official saying reviews found gaps in their disclosures. The House passed the DETERRENT Act (H.R. 1048) on 2025-03-27 (241 to 169) to lower the reporting threshold to $50,000 and add Title IV funding penalties; it has not passed the Senate. No source found shows a university losing accreditation, a charter or federal funding for taking Chinese party money.

timeline.event: The House passes the DETERRENT Act (H.R. 1048) by 241 to 169: it would lower the foreign gift reporting threshold from $250,000 to $50,000 (zero for countries of concern) and impose penalties including fines and loss of Title IV funding for noncompliance; it was referred to the Senate HELP Committee.

President signs Executive Order 14282 (published 2025-04-28): the Education Secretary is to enforce Section 117 with the Attorney General, compliance certification is to be treated as material under the False Claims Act, and federal grant funds are not to go to noncompliant institutions. The text does not mention accreditation.

The Education Department opens a Section 117 investigation into UC Berkeley over alleged failure to disclose foreign funding, citing reports of hundreds of millions of dollars from a foreign government; a 2023 report put undisclosed Chinese government money at $220 million, and the university denies the claim.

The Education Department launches an updated Section 117 reporting portal; on 2026-02-11 it announces 11 new data elements and published data on about 8,300 transactions worth over $5.2 billion, and on 2026-02-20 it signs an interagency agreement with the State Department to oversee reporting, enforcement and compliance.

The Education Department releases new data on foreignfundinghighered.gov showing that several universities received gifts or signed contracts with entities the U.S. government lists as national security concerns; the House China committee release names no universities and no penalties.

title: Cut universities taking Chinese Communist Party money from accreditation and funds
uncertainties: The Foreword's three penalties (accreditation, charters, federal funds) are not all reachable by federal action; the sources show only disclosure enforcement and investigations, and the grant bar in Executive Order 14282 applies to disclosure noncompliance rather than to accepting Chinese party money. The Berkeley investigation was announced on Friday 2025-04-25 (U.S. time) per a report dated the next day. The Duke and North Dakota report gives no detail on the scope of the probe or any penalty, and no Education or State Department release on it was found. The Debevoise alert is a law-firm summary of Education Department actions, not the Department documents; it dates the State Department agreement 2026-02-20 while its linked file name refers to 2026-02-23. The House bill's penalty terms are from the sponsor's press release, not the bill text. Whether any institution has lost Title IV eligibility or grants over Section 117 was searched only in a limited way and none was found. Related records c11-10 (accreditation) and c21-03 carry adjacent material.
